content: Visine is a brand of eye drops manufactured by Johnson & Johnson. The company acquired Visine, along with Pfizer's entire consumer healthcare portfolio, in December 2006. The active ingredients in the original Visine formulation are potassium chloride and tetrahydrozoline hydrochloride. Tetrahydrozoline hydrochloride acts as a vasoconstrictor, meaning it narrows the superficial blood vessels in the eye. This mechanism is intended to reduce redness, as advertised by Johnson & Johnson with the slogan get the red out. Visine is applied topically, like other eye drops. The recommended dosage is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) up to four times daily. Frequent users of Visine Original often report stinging and burning sensations upon application. Additionally, prolonged use can lead to a rebound effect, where the redness of the eyes worsens after the initial effect wears off. Chronic use may result in permanent dilation of the blood vessels in the eye. Therefore, the use of Visine should be limited. It is important to note that red eyes can sometimes indicate more serious underlying ocular conditions. Simply reducing blood flow to the area will not address the root cause of the condition and may even exacerbate symptoms. Furthermore, these drops are not recommended for individuals who wear contact lenses. The vasoconstrictive effect reduces blood flow to the surface of the eye, which can further decrease oxygen levels available to the eye, potentially causing additional complications.
